How Healthy Are Beets?

Their eye-popping colors will give you a hint.

By Simar Bajaj

Aug. 10, 2026 Leer en español

Beets have a reputation as a health food, and the pigment that stains your cutting board is part of the reason. TOKEN_BEETS_BODY Those betalains are antioxidants, and the roots also bring folate, potassium, and a dose of dietary nitrate that some studies link to lower blood pressure and steadier exercise. The greens are edible too, closer to chard than to a garnish.

Roasting concentrates the sugar and keeps the color. A tray of wedges with olive oil and salt is enough. TOKEN_BEETS_RECIPE If you pickle them, the vinegar brightens the earthiness without hiding it. A blender of cooked beets, chickpeas, lemon, and garlic makes a hummus that stays magenta for days.

Doctors still tell people on certain blood-pressure drugs to be thoughtful about extra nitrate, and anyone who has had oxalate kidney stones should not treat beet juice as a daily tonic. For everyone else, the vegetable is food, not a supplement. Eat the roots you like, keep the greens, and ignore the wellness claims that outrun the evidence.
